item.title: in a cafe
item.author: hey@stefanmiko.com (Stefan Mikolajczyk)

item.content:encoded:
We’re in the week after the new year (têt) holiday in Vietnam.

The city is calm, restful. Streets are breathing, enjoying a pause for a few days before life comes at them again.

Most places are closed, people are spending time with their family and enjoying time off work. Some cafés are still open and stay the best place to get a feeling for the city, its people, get inspired and work a bit.

I’m sitting on a table surrounded by others around me. This position could feel vulnerable, but it feels great here. In front of me I see people studying on their own, sipping away at a fruity tea. On my left is a couple of younger teens, dressed almost identically, studying but also talking a lot with one another. It’s hard for them to keep studying when the appeal of looking into each other’s eyes is here. They decide that they should maybe go, it’s been a few hours they are here and they’re obviously not advancing on their original objective anymore.

Behind me I hear a conversation, louder than the usual very quiet cafe crowd. I glance over and it looks like a teacher and their students working on their Vietnamese pronunciation. They’re repeating the same few words over and over.

Meanwhile the staff is preparing, serving and cleaning various drinks, while it’s late afternoon now, coffee seems to still be a favourite choice and embalms the room into a motivating aroma.

Today doesn’t really feel like a holiday but it feels like a great day.

item.title: building a house
item.author: hey@stefanmiko.com (Stefan Mikolajczyk)
item.description: Reading through Kening Zhu’s journal was a flash in the mirror moment. Seeing someone confidently develop their own space on the internet. Finding myself curious and passionate about exploring all pages, taking in ideas and inspiration. I hadn’t experienced that on the internet in a while. At one point I probably had 25 tabs opened trying to take it all in, but also getting excited to not, not wanting to spoil it all, and just browsing at my own pace.
item.content:encoded:
Reading through Kening Zhu’s journal was a flash in the mirror moment.

Seeing someone confidently develop their own space on the internet. Finding myself curious and passionate about exploring all pages, taking in ideas and inspiration. I hadn’t experienced that on the internet in a while.

At one point I probably had 25 tabs opened trying to take it all in, but also getting excited to not, not wanting to spoil it all, and just browsing at my own pace.

This felt like a great moment, I want to build this house in 2025.

I want to find a space where my work, art, thoughts and journey can live.

This is a space I would want to talk about art, social issues, my growth through the world, the work and the people I meet.

This feels right.

item.title: fiction aspirer
item.author: hey@stefanmiko.com (Stefan Mikolajczyk)
item.description: Writing documentation makes you shed all the fluff. Any words unnecessary to a description, any words unnecessary to make you understood. You delete. I like this writing style, it’s pragmatic, it’s very in line with coding, simple is better. But I also aspire to write fiction, which requires the fluff (I think). I’m spending my days writing in a way that can’t be used for my other projects. It’s hard to reconcile, sometimes.
item.content:encoded:
Writing documentation makes you shed all the fluff.
Any words unnecessary to a description, any words unnecessary to make you understood.
You delete.

I like this writing style, it’s pragmatic, it’s very in line with coding, simple is better.
But I also aspire to write fiction, which requires the fluff (I think).

I’m spending my days writing in a way that can’t be used for my other projects.
It’s hard to reconcile, sometimes.

item.title: not for me
item.author: hey@stefanmiko.com (Stefan Mikolajczyk)
item.description: After almost two years of contract work. This is the first time that I have said no to work. The first client I am okay not building a relationship with. item.content:encoded:
After almost two years of contract work.
This is the first time that I have said no to work.

The first client I am okay not building a relationship with.
There’s nothing inherently wrong with what was proposed nor the interaction we had.

I’ve delivered a first project.
There was a lot of work ahead, a promise of a regular income and a long term client.

Clients like them I usually sought. Their stability reassuring me while I kept whatever freedom this is.
This time it felt a bit different. I saw myself finishing the first contract, marking a pause, not rushing to the next.

Trusted my gut and said “I won’t continue”.
The yes man of the rat race died that day.

Odd and liberating.
